name: Stomach vacuum / waist training

card.summary: Pulling the belly in to train the deep abdominal muscle for a smaller-looking waist; little research exists on it for appearance.
card.note: Sources on abdominal exercise say it does not by itself reduce abdominal fat.

quick.overview:
The stomach vacuum is an exercise in which the abdomen is drawn inward, aimed at the transversus abdominis, the deepest abdominal muscle. Forum users discuss it as a way to get a tighter-looking waist.

Sources are thin. A looksmax.org thread has a user asking whether others lost the ability to do it and reporting it came back with renewed training.
quick.mechanism: The transversus abdominis is one of four abdominal wall muscles. Wikipedia notes that whether training this deep core muscle specifically is worthwhile is disputed, and that abdominal exercise alone is not enough to reduce abdominal fat or girth according to a 2011 study.
quick.risks: No harms data were found for the exercise. Community talk of 'waist training' sometimes also refers to compression garments, which this entry does not cover.

lead: The stomach vacuum is an abdominal exercise in which the belly button is drawn inward toward the spine by contracting the deep abdominal muscles, mainly the transversus abdominis, with little use of the diaphragm.[3] People practice it for a flatter, tighter-looking midsection and a smaller apparent waist; Wikipedia says it is used for a leaner midsection in bodybuilding competitions.[3]

The transversus abdominis is the deepest of the flat abdominal muscles and is often called the corset muscle because pulling the abdomen inward creates girdle-like tension around the midsection.[4] Looksmaxxing discussion treats training it as a way to improve waist appearance without compression garments.

Community material is limited to short forum posts, such as a looksmax.org thread in which a user says he nearly lost the ability to perform it two years earlier and can do it easily again after resuming training.[2] No clinical studies were found.

paras: Wikipedia describes the vacuum exercise as contracting the internal abdominal muscles, with repetitions that can serve as light aerobic or light strength work.[3] Strength can be built, it says, by drawing the muscle in further, contracting harder or holding longer, and some people use a string tied at navel level as feedback.[3] Wikipedia also notes disputed benefit and healthiness of doing it while lifting.[3]

The abdominal exercise article describes the transversus abdominis as part of the four-muscle abdominal wall and says focused training of this deep core muscle is disputed, with some experts recommending broader regimens.[1]

The phrase waist training is also used for wearing compression garments such as corsets; this entry concerns the muscle exercise. Related practices include hypopressive exercises, which Wikipedia says are thought to raise abdominal wall and pelvic floor tone and reduce resting waist circumference.[3]

The abdominal exercise article states that whether abdominal exercise reduces belly fat is highly disputed, citing a 2011 study that found abdominal exercises alone were not enough to reduce abdominal fat and girth, and adds that fat reduction requires an energy deficit.[1] Wikipedia notes that the effectiveness of transversus abdominis training is debated, with some reviews finding its function does not reliably predict low back pain outcomes.[4]

lore.intro: Discussion on looksmax.org is brief and anecdotal [2].

claims.claim: The stomach vacuum skill can be lost and regained with training.
claims.believers: One user reports that he could barely do it two years earlier and can do it easily after training again [2].
claims.experts: No published studies have examined this.

chain: Draw the belly inward with deep abdominal contraction
Transversus abdominis (the corset muscle) gets trained
angle.text: Practitioners use the stomach vacuum to build control of the deep abdominal wall so the waist and stomach look tighter. The change is in muscle tone and posture of the midsection rather than in body fat.
